script.source:
//@version=5
indicator("uct-sma-ema-parity-v1", overlay=false)
sma20 = ta.sma(close, 20)
ema20 = ta.ema(close, 20)
plot(sma20, title="sma20")
plot(ema20, title="ema20")

provenance.note: Captured via CSV export (Table view -> Download data) of a real SPY Daily chart with a live ta.sma(close,20)/ta.ema(close,20) indicator added, full double-precision floats. 2,031 real trading-day bars (2018-08-07..2026-09-04). ema(close,20) is SMA-of-first-window-seeded, exponentially-recursive (matching Pine's own documented ta.ema convention exactly -- no known formula-convention divergence the way atr has) -- but, like rsi/atr, it is expected to show the SAME capture-window cold-start seed-convergence lag (a leaky IIR filter re-seeds at THIS window's own first bar, while the real vendor value already reflects continuous smoothing since SPY's real 1993 inception). See _vendor_parity_warmup_bars_note for the measured boundary.

_vendor_parity_warmup_bars_note: 100 is NOT the semantic period-warmup (that is 19 bars -- the first index at which ema(close,20) is computable at all). It is a conservative round number past the empirically observed convergence point (last disagreeing index measured at 92 of 2031) for the SAME general capture-window cold-start effect already documented for rsi/atr (divergences.json::recursive-smoother-cold-start-in-a-finite-capture) -- EMA converges much faster than the Wilder/RMA-seeded functions (its SMA-of-first-window seed starts much closer to the true long-run value: 0.14% relative at bar 19 vs rsi/atr's 12-25% at bar 14) but the SAME underlying mechanism applies: a leaky exponential filter re-seeds cold at this capture window's own first bar, while the real vendor value already reflects decades of continuous smoothing. Bars 100+ (1,931 of 2,031) never disagree again.
